narratives.Overview:
1. Router boundary. In `packages/runtime/src/cli-router/route-argv.ts`, every `kind: "dispatch"` result of `routeArgv` passes through one function before it is returned. The function returns the result unchanged when its argv is empty, when the routed head `argv[0]` is `scm`, or when the head is a meta form (`--help`, `-h`, `help`, `--version`, `-V`); stub results are also returned unchanged. Otherwise it finds the boundary: index 2 when the head is a subcommand handler and `argv[1]` is a word (not empty and not starting with `-`), otherwise index 1. The subcommand handlers are the first elements of the `SUBCOMMAND_ROUTES` values, plus `scope-lifecycle`; the function derives the set from that exported table. If the token at the boundary is exactly `--`, it removes that one token and keeps every other token. It reuses `dropLeadingDoubleDash` (still exported from `dispatch.ts`) on the arguments after the boundary. Examples (parent prototype on the real `routeArgv`): `cache:clear -- --x` gives `["cache","clear","--x"]`; `vbrief reconcile graph -- --x` gives `["vbrief-reconcile","graph","--x"]`; `vbrief reconcile -- --all` gives `["vbrief-reconcile","--all"]`; `vbrief reconcile parity -- --all` gives `["vbrief-reconcile","parity","--all"]`; `policy resolve -- --project-root x` gives `["policy","resolve","--project-root","x"]`; `triage-queue --limit -- 3` is unchanged; `verify orphan-active -- --issue 7` gives `["verify:orphan-active","--issue","7"]`; `policy:show -- --x` gives `["policy:show","--x"]` and `dispatch` then inserts `show`; `scm:body:issue:fetch -- --x` gives `["github-body","issue-fetch","--x"]`; `policy set f -- --y` and `scm issue list -- --limit 1` are unchanged. Why a word is safe: every subcommand handler refuses or ignores a word that is not one of its subcommands, so dropping a `--` after it never turns a refused or ignored call into different work. Parent runs through the real `routeAndDispatch` of `<handler> zzz -- --no-such-flag` and `<handler> zzz --no-such-flag` for all 13 handlers: each exits non-zero in both forms. `slice` refuses the word (`packages/core/src/slice/cli.ts` 144, `unrecognized arguments: zzz`); `triage-queue` ignores a word and already skips every `--` (`packages/runtime/src/triage-queue.ts` 147, 234); `vbrief-reconcile`, `cache`, `policy`, `authz`, `escalation-cli`, `product-signal`, `github-body` and `scope-lifecycle` refuse it as an unknown subcommand; `triage-actions`, `triage-bulk` and `plan-sequence` refuse it as an unknown subcommand or action (parent runs of `<handler> zzz`, `<handler> zzz x` and `<handler> zzz -- x` all exit 2). Shorthand targets that are words but not subcommands, `grant-*` for `authz revoke` and `esc-*` for `escalation resolve`, are safe too: both parsers already strip a following `--` (audit 7070758592, finding 2). Handlers outside this set, such as `vbrief-validate` with its `conformance` subcommand, are not covered; the operator moved them to #6944.
2. Dispatcher. `dispatch` no longer drops a `--` (the `dropLeadingDoubleDash(rawRest)` call added by #6910 is removed, so `rest` is `rawRest`). One invocation therefore loses at most one `--`. Per-verb parsers are not edited.
3. Real-router test. Extend `packages/runtime/src/dispatch-double-dash-real-parser.test.ts` (real `routeAndDispatch`, empty temporary directory, dispatch io and process streams captured, nothing stubbed, no `--help`): `["cache:clear","--no-such-flag"]` and `["cache:clear","--","--no-such-flag"]` both exit 1 with the same output (`cmdClear` has no value check, so an unknown flag is its refuse-before-work form: it throws before `clearTaskCache`); `["policy","show","--format=invalid"]` and `["policy","show","--","--format=invalid"]` both exit 2 with the same output (`policy: invalid choice: 'invalid'`, from `parseShowArgs` before any read); `["policy","resolve","--project-root"]` and `["policy","resolve","--","--project-root"]` both exit 2 with the same output (`policy: argument --project-root: expected one argument`, from `parseProjectRoot` before `runResolve`); `["review-monitor:register","--","--","--pr=abc"]` exits 2 with `unrecognized argument: --` (no second drop); `["triage-queue","--limit","--","3"]` exits 2 with `argument --limit: invalid int value: '--'` (the `--` that is a flag value reaches the parser; `runQueue` returns on the parse error before resolving a repo). The two #6910 pairs stay as regression checks. The cache, policy show and policy resolve pairs fail without items 1-2 (parent runs: the `--` forms exit with `unexpected argument: --` and `unrecognized argument: --`).
4. Router-only test. A vitest file for `routeArgv` alone, with no handler run: (a) for every `SUBCOMMAND_ROUTES` key with exactly one colon, in the colon spelling and the space spelling `[ns, verb]`, and for every `SCOPE_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` entry as `scope:<v>` and `scope-<v>`: `[...form, "--", "--x"]` routes to the same argv as `[...form, "--x"]`, and `[...form, "--", "--", "--x"]` keeps exactly one `--`; (b) exact expected argv for every item 1 example, for `review-monitor:register -- --pr 1`, `check -- --x`, and `cache:clear --x -- y` (a later `--` is kept); (c) `scm issue list -- --limit 1`, `policy set f -- --y`, `triage-queue --limit -- 3` and `--help` route unchanged. This covers every router-chosen subcommand route plus named forms; it does not claim every possible spelling.
5. Docs: none. The #6910 helper tests stay; only their comments that say `dispatch` applies the helper are updated to name the router.

Parent check of items 1, 3 and 4. The parent ran a throwaway prototype of the item 1 rule on top of the real `routeArgv` (tsx, router source equal to the dispatch SHA, no repo edit). Every item 1 example routed as stated. The item 4(a) sweep (170 forms: both spellings of every one-colon `SUBCOMMAND_ROUTES` key and both spellings of every scope lifecycle verb) gave the same argv with and without `--` and kept exactly one `--` from `-- --`; without the rule, the `--` stays in every one of those routed forms. The parent also ran the item 3 calls and the 13-handler stray-word calls through the real `routeAndDispatch` from an empty temporary directory on the current tree (router blob equal to the dispatch SHA; dispatch and test blobs equal to the #6910 head), with the results stated in items 1 and 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `deft cache:clear -- --project-root <dir>` and `deft cache:clear --project-root <dir>` give the cache handler the same arguments.
- `routeArgv` drops at most one lone `--`, at the first token after the routed head, or after the next token when the head is a subcommand handler (a first element of a `SUBCOMMAND_ROUTES` value, or `scope-lifecycle`) and that token is a word not starting with `-`; it keeps every other token, leaves `scm` results, meta forms and stubs unchanged, and `dispatch` no longer drops a `--`.
- `deft vbrief reconcile -- --all` routes to `vbrief-reconcile --all`, `deft policy resolve -- --project-root <dir>` routes to `policy resolve --project-root <dir>`, and `deft triage-queue --limit -- 3` keeps its `--` as the flag value.
- `deft verify orphan-active -- --issue <N>`, the `scope:promote`, `scope:activate` and `scope:complete` forms with `--`, `review-monitor:register -- ...`, `occupancy:release -- ...`, `policy:show -- ...` and `check -- ...` keep working, and `deft policy set <field> -- ...`, `deft scm issue <sub> -- ...` and `deft vbrief validate conformance -- ...` (moved to #6944) are unchanged.
- A vitest test runs the real `routeAndDispatch` from an empty temporary directory with nothing stubbed and no `--help`, and asserts that `cache:clear --no-such-flag` and `cache:clear -- --no-such-flag` exit 1 with the same output, that `policy show --format=invalid` and `policy show -- --format=invalid` exit 2 with the same output, that `policy resolve --project-root` and `policy resolve -- --project-root` exit 2 with the same output, that `review-monitor:register -- -- --pr=abc` exits 2 with `unrecognized argument: --`, and that `triage-queue --limit -- 3` exits 2 with `argument --limit: invalid int value: '--'`.
- A `routeArgv` test asserts that every one-colon `SUBCOMMAND_ROUTES` key (colon and space spellings) and every scope lifecycle verb (`scope:<v>` and `scope-<v>`) routes the same with and without a lone `--` and keeps exactly one `--` from `-- --`, checks exact argv for `cache:clear`, `vbrief reconcile graph`, `vbrief reconcile -- --all`, `vbrief reconcile parity`, `policy resolve`, `verify orphan-active`, `policy:show`, `scm:body:issue:fetch`, `review-monitor:register`, `check` and a later `--`, and checks that `scm issue list -- ...`, `policy set <field> -- ...` and `triage-queue --limit -- 3` route unchanged.
narratives.Constraint:
- Dropping the `--` for every route, `scm` included (comment 7052439964, finding 1): `scm issue <sub>` forwards it to `gh`, where it ends options.
- Dropping only where each route stops reading its arguments (comment 7052439964, finding 2): `vbrief reconcile graph -- ...` is routed with `graph` among the arguments, so the drop would miss it.
- Moving three-token matching ahead of namespace matching (comment 7052439964, finding 2): it would also turn `policy set <field>` into a subcommand form.
- Claiming the router-only test covers every spelling (comment 7052439964, finding 3): it covers every router-chosen subcommand route and named forms only.
- Using a `routeArgv`-equality sweep as the #6897 guard (comment 7052439964, answer 5): it does not run the real parser; #6897 stays deferred.
- Choosing index 2 from the handler name alone (comment 7052513274, finding 1): `vbrief reconcile -- --all` would keep its `--`, and `triage-queue --limit -- 3` would lose a flag value.
- Recognising a subcommand only from the router tables (comment 7070655127, finding 1): `policy resolve` is a real subcommand no table names, so its `--` would stay.
- Adding a `policy:resolve` route to the table (comment 7070655127, finding 1): it adds a public alias and still misses the next unlisted subcommand.

## In plain English
#6887 (PR #6910, not yet merged) makes `deft <verb> -- args` work for one-word verbs: the dispatcher drops one leading `--`. Commands that the router expands into a handler plus a subcommand still fail. `deft cache:clear -- --project-root <dir>` becomes `cache clear -- --project-root <dir>`, the `--` is no longer first when the dispatcher looks, and the cache parser refuses it. The same happens to `deft policy show -- ...` and `deft slice:list -- ...`.

The recommended fix moves the drop into the router, the one place that knows where the command words end and the user's arguments begin. The router drops one lone `--` right there for every route, and the dispatcher stops dropping, so `-- -- x` still keeps its second `--`. Tests run the real router and real parsers with a bad argument, so each parser refuses before doing any work, and check that the forms with and without `--` give the same result. A cheap router-only check covers every subcommand route.

Pain source: the three pains are the issue's `## Acceptance Criteria` items as written.

## Pains
- P1 — `deft cache:clear -- --project-root <dir>` and the form without `--` give the handler the same arguments.
- P2 — The drop happens once, at the boundary between the routed verb tokens and the user arguments, for every multi-token namespace form; a later `--` is kept.
- P3 — A real-router test (no stubs) covers at least `cache:clear` and one other multi-token namespace with and without `--`.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- The every-documented-verb guard test (#6897). It stays deferred unless the critic finds the router-only check below closes it cheaply; changing or closing #6897 would be an operator decision.
- Launcher-owned verbs (`install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `doctor` in `packages/cli`), and how the host hook classifies `deft <verb> -- ...`. Unchanged.
- A `--` after a handler's own first argument, for example `deft policy set <field> -- ...`: the router routes `policy set` to `policy-set` and passes `<field>` as an argument (parent `routeArgv` run), so that `--` is not at the boundary. Unchanged.
- Parsers that already skip every `--` (scope, triage-queue, plan-sequence, the policy `set-*` parsers). Not edited.
- Meta forms (`--help`, `help`, `--version`). Unchanged.

## Constraints (not pains)
- One small PR for the next build, after #6910 merges (it builds on the #6910 helper `dropLeadingDoubleDash`). No new gate, refusal, verb, flag or stored file. Per-verb parsers are not edited.
- `task <verb> -- <args>` keeps working (go-task removes the `--`).
- `deft verify orphan-active -- --issue N`, the `scope:promote` / `scope:activate` / `scope:complete` forms with `--`, and the #6910 single-token forms (`review-monitor:register`, `occupancy:release`) keep working.
